Alpine.js is part of 7 of my public repositories, from 2024 to 2026.

What it was for: [Science and visualisation](@/projects/science.md) (2), [Tools](@/projects/tools.md) (2), [Knowledge](@/projects/knowledge.md) (1) and [Media and art](@/projects/media.md) (1).

Most recently: [Kompendium](@/work/kompendium-epistemicke-anihilace.md): A book, a website and a wiki: mechanisms, detection signatures, defence and recovery, cross-linked into a graph you can explore; [korczis.github.io](@/work/korczis-github-io.md): Tomas Korcak (korczis): software that proves its work. Projects, live sites and the stack behind them. Zola + Flowbite Pro on GitHub Pages, supervised by Majordomus; [Oscilla](@/work/oscilla.md): Generate, measure and reproduce sound experiments, and know how far each result can be trusted. Every readout carries its uncertainty.

6 of these projects run as live sites.

I also used it in client work under confidentiality agreements. Roles: Architect, Lead engineer, AI engineer and Data engineer. What was solved: LLM agents, Decision support, AI transformation and Audit trail. The use cases below give the principle and the intent of that work; no client, person, date or number is named.

How to read the evidence: every [repository](@/glossary/repository.md) below is measured from GitHub and GitLab (every 6 hours) and says how it uses Alpine.js: as the main language, as a measured share of its code, in its declared stack or as a topic. The reference graph links Alpine.js to the repositories and to the other languages and technologies they use together.
